Aug 23, 2026 Manouk Akopyan Aug 23, 2026 2 min read Rolando Romero was a man of few words after his majority decision defeat against Teofimo Lopez on Saturday at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. He had no interest in talking about what had just transpired, having lost the WBA welterweight title . "I'd like to just thank my lord and savior Jesus Christ for everything in my life that I have got to enjoy. I will always be your faithful servant," Romero said before abruptly leaving the ring. Scores of 116-112 and 115-113 saw Romero (17-3, 13 KOs) beaten for the third time in little over four years, despite a third judge having it a draw at 114-114. It can definitely be argued the scorecards were generous for the now-former beltholder, who was outlanded 124-to-73 according to CompuBox. Romero enjoyed the best sequence of a mostly unspectacular fight in the fifth, stunning Lopez with a right hand and buckling his knees in the final minute of the round, 20 seconds after slicing Lopez's eyebrow with a left hook. Romero unleashed a hellacious flurry, but Lopez survived the round and immediately got back in the driver's seat for the remainder of their meeting. Romero landed double digits in punches in only one round round five according to CompuBox and lacked the urgency to stave off the surging Lopez beginning in the sixth. Even Romero's trainer Ismael Salas implored his charge to dial up the pressure to ensure victory would be within reach. During his post-fight press conference, Romero elaborated on the sequence of events that led to the loss following a career-best unanimous decision win against Ryan Garcia 15 months ago . "My immediate thoughts, look at my face. I got hit with what, two clean shots the whole fight," Romero said. "If that's enough to beat the champion, that's enough. "He never hurt me at any given moment. He got hurt multiple times throughout the fight. Every time I threw a shot, I landed it. He couldn't land anything clean on me, it was clear and apparent. "I could have pressed more. Of course, anyone can but you know, championship fights, they're all close like this, especially with two high-level fighters." Romero also elaborated on the dramatic fifth round, which saw Lopez touch the canvas during a hellacious sequence. Referee Harvey Dock ruled it a slip. "Honestly, it should have been counted as a knockdown, but you know how it is," Romero said. "He survived, knows how to survive. I hit him so many times clean and hurt him. Some of those rounds were for sure 10-8 rounds. "I was trying to open that cut even more, more than anything. I was trying to feint and land a good left hand. "I couldn't get him clean. He didn't completely wobble. The other shot I hit him with at the end of the round, though, he was out." Nov 16, 2025 The Ring Staff Nov 16, 2025 0 min read Conor Benn did exactly as he promised, avenging his career-first professional defeat, and did so without much difficulty against an underwhelming Chris Eubank Jr performance. Seven months after their initial meeting, Chris Eubank Jr. and Conor Benn headlined Tottenham Hotspur Stadium once more with a markedly different outcome than their thrilling April firefight. Benn (24-1, 14 KOs) began sharp and outlanded the older man across all 12 rounds, connecting on more body punches (70) than Eubank managed total (68) per the CompuBox numbers, as the 29-year-old avenged defeat and floored him twice in the final frame. 119-107, 116-110 and 118-108 read the three scorecards on an evening where Benn's adjustments paid dividends while Eubank (35-4, 25 KOs) must now ask difficult questions of his fighting future after being far less active and firmly second best from minute one. Dec 7, 2025 The Ring Staff Dec 7, 2025 1 min read Making his second weight jump in as many fights, now-former 130-pound world champion Lamont Roach's divisional debut was full of milestones as he withstood Isaac Cruz's early attacks to finish strong in the second-half of an absorbing interim WBC junio... Lamont Roach recovered from a third-round knockdown to outwork Isaac Cruz in the second-half of a competitive 12-round clash, but the now-former WBA 130-pound world champion didn't do enough in the judges' eyes to edge their WBC interim junior welterweight title clash. During an absorbing clash, Cruz held a narrow 87-85 edge in punches landed through five rounds, as well as scoring a 10-8 in the third frame after connecting on a left hook to leave Roach scrambling to stay upright - surrendering the first knockdown of his 11-year career. Yet after round five, the tide turned in the Maryland man's favor. Making his divisional debut at 140-pounds here, he connected on 49% of his power punches, almost doubled Cruz's landed jab tally (49-27) and had more success with round-by-round output preceding the final frame, which saw the Mexican just do enough - despite having a point deducted in the seventh. Chris Tellez scored it 115-111 for Cruz, while judges Nathan Palmer and Cory A Santos both had it 113-113 on a night neither will forget anytime soon as they look to 2026 and another potential rematch. Aug 16, 2025 The Ring Staff Aug 16, 2025 0 min read It was all too easy for Ring ambassador Hayato Tsutsumi during his Saudi showcase against Britain's Qais Ashfaq, but what did the punch stats say through three rounds? Two fights, two third-round finishes in 2025 for Ring ambassador Hayato Tsutsumi after quickly proving too hot to handle for Qais Ashfaq during their junior lightweight matchup. The 26-year-old quickly got to work against the seven-year southpaw, making the British underdog work hard during a competitive opening round evidenced by their closely-contested punch stats -- Tsutsumi threw four more total punches (24-20) and landed five more. His striking success only increased as time wore on, much to Ashfaq's drastic demise, with 17 of his 22 connected punches being credited as power punches in a second stanza which saw the 31-year-old floored and increasingly frustrated. It wouldn't last much longer. 74.1% connect percentage on power punches speaks for itself during a dominant third round and mercifully, veteran referee Leszek Jankowiak had seen enough at 2:08 of the frame. Jul 19, 2025 The Ring Staff Jul 19, 2025 0 min read The post-fight headlines will feature viral pictures of Daniel Lapin twice hanging off the ropes like a superhero, though he won't mind. The post-fight headlines will feature viral pictures of Daniel Lapin twice hanging off the ropes like a superhero, though he won't mind. The surging Ukrainian contender came to Wembley and seized an unbeaten record while importantly keeping his own intact after a 10-round majority decision win (95-95, 96-94, 96-94) over British light-heavyweight champion Lewis Edmondson . He connected on a fight-high 24 punches in the penultimate round, having almost fallen over the top rope twice in the stanza beforehand. Such was their messy affair, it shouldn't be a surprise to know Lapin only landed 30 power punches up to the seventh round - though excelled when he needed to under duress, outlanding The Saint 39-13 over the last six minutes.
